paragraphs.text: Now there was a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews:
paragraphs.original: Ἦν δὲ ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τῶν Φαρισαίων, Νικόδημος ὄνομα αὐτῷ, ἄρχων τῶν Ἰουδαίων·
paragraphs.translit: Ēn de anthrōpos ek tōn Pharisaiōn, Nikodēmos onoma autō, archōn tōn Ioudaiōn·

paragraphs.text: the same came unto him by night, and said to him, Rabbi, we know that thou art a teacher come from God; for no one can do these signs that thou doest, except God be with him.
paragraphs.original: οὗτος ἦλθεν πρὸς αὐτὸν νυκτὸς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ῥαββί, οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀπὸ θεοῦ ἐλήλυθας διδάσκαλος· οὐδεὶς γὰρ δύναται ταῦτα τὰ σημεῖα ποιεῖν ἃ σὺ ποιεῖς, ἐὰν μὴ ᾖ ὁ θεὸς μετʼ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: houtos ēlthen pros auton nyktos kai eipen autō· Rhabbi, oidamen hoti apo theou elēlythas didaskalos· oudeis gar dynatai tauta ta sēmeia poiein ha sy poieis, ean mē ē ho theos metʼ autou.

paragraphs.text: Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except one be born anew, he cannot see the kingdom of God.
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω σοι, ἐὰν μή τις γεννηθῇ ἄνωθεν, οὐ δύναται ἰδεῖν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē Iēsous kai eipen autō· Amēn amēn legō soi, ean mē tis gennēthē anōthen, ou dynatai idein tēn basileian tou theou.

paragraphs.text: Nicodemus saith unto him, How can a man be born when he is old? can he enter a second time into his mother`s womb, and be born?
paragraphs.original: λέγει πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ Νικόδημος· Πῶς δύναται ἄνθρωπος γεννηθῆναι γέρων ὤν; μὴ δύναται εἰς τὴν κοιλίαν τῆς μητρὸς αὐτοῦ δεύτερον εἰσελθεῖν καὶ γεννηθῆναι;
paragraphs.translit: legei pros auton ho Nikodēmos· Pōs dynatai anthrōpos gennēthēnai gerōn ōn; mē dynatai eis tēn koilian tēs mētros autou deuteron eiselthein kai gennēthēnai;

paragraphs.text: Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except one be born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God!
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς· Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω σοι, ἐὰν μή τις γεννηθῇ ἐξ ὕδατος καὶ πνεύματος, οὐ δύναται εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē Iēsous· Amēn amēn legō soi, ean mē tis gennēthē ex hydatos kai pneumatos, ou dynatai eiselthein eis tēn basileian tou theou.

paragraphs.text: That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.
paragraphs.original: τὸ γεγεννημένον ἐκ τῆς σαρκὸς σάρξ ἐστιν, καὶ τὸ γεγεννημένον ἐκ τοῦ πνεύματος πνεῦμά ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: to gegennēmenon ek tēs sarkos sarx estin, kai to gegennēmenon ek tou pneumatos pneuma estin.

paragraphs.text: Marvel not that I said unto thee, Ye must be born anew.
paragraphs.original: μὴ θαυμάσῃς ὅτι εἶπόν σοι Δεῖ ὑμᾶς γεννηθῆναι ἄνωθεν.
paragraphs.translit: mē thaumasēs hoti eipon soi Dei hymas gennēthēnai anōthen.

paragraphs.text: The wind bloweth where it will, and thou hearest the voice thereof, but knowest not whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.
paragraphs.original: τὸ πνεῦμα ὅπου θέλει πνεῖ, καὶ τὴν φωνὴν αὐτοῦ ἀκούεις, ἀλλʼ οὐκ οἶδας πόθεν ἔρχεται καὶ ποῦ ὑπάγει· οὕτως ἐστὶν πᾶς ὁ γεγεννημένος ἐκ τοῦ πνεύματος.
paragraphs.translit: to pneuma hopou thelei pnei, kai tēn phōnēn autou akoueis, allʼ ouk oidas pothen erchetai kai pou hypagei· houtōs estin pas ho gegennēmenos ek tou pneumatos.

paragraphs.text: Nicodemus answered and said unto him, How can these things be?
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη Νικόδημος καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Πῶς δύναται ταῦτα γενέσθαι;
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē Nikodēmos kai eipen autō· Pōs dynatai tauta genesthai;

paragraphs.text: Jesus answered and said unto him, Art thou the teacher of Israel, and understandest not these things?
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Σὺ εἶ ὁ διδάσκαλος τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ καὶ ταῦτα οὐ γινώσκεις;
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē Iēsous kai eipen autō· Sy ei ho didaskalos tou Israēl kai tauta ou ginōskeis;

paragraphs.text: Verily, verily, I say unto thee, We speak that which we know, and bear witness of that which we have seen; and ye receive not our witness.
paragraphs.original: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω σοι ὅτι ὃ οἴδαμεν λαλοῦμεν καὶ ὃ ἑωράκαμεν μαρτυροῦμεν, καὶ τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἡμῶν οὐ λαμβάνετε.
paragraphs.translit: amēn amēn legō soi hoti ho oidamen laloumen kai ho heōrakamen martyroumen, kai tēn martyrian hēmōn ou lambanete.

paragraphs.text: If I told you earthly things and ye believe not, how shall ye believe if I tell you heavenly things?
paragraphs.original: εἰ τὰ ἐπίγεια εἶπον ὑμῖν καὶ οὐ πιστεύετε, πῶς ἐὰν εἴπω ὑμῖν τὰ ἐπουράνια πιστεύσετε;
paragraphs.translit: ei ta epigeia eipon hymin kai ou pisteuete, pōs ean eipō hymin ta epourania pisteusete;

paragraphs.text: And no one hath ascended into heaven, but he that descended out of heaven, [even] the Son of man, who is in heaven.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐδεὶς ἀναβέβηκεν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εἰ μὴ ὁ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβάς, ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
paragraphs.translit: kai oudeis anabebēken eis ton ouranon ei mē ho ek tou ouranou katabas, ho hyios tou anthrōpou.

paragraphs.text: And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up;
paragraphs.original: καὶ καθὼς Μωϋσῆς ὕψωσεν τὸν ὄφιν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, οὕτως ὑψωθῆναι δεῖ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου,
paragraphs.translit: kai kathōs Mōysēs hypsōsen ton ophin en tē erēmō, houtōs hypsōthēnai dei ton hyion tou anthrōpou,

paragraphs.text: that whosoever believeth may in him have eternal life.
paragraphs.original: ἵνα πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων ἐν αὐτῷ ἔχῃ ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
paragraphs.translit: hina pas ho pisteuōn en autō echē zōēn aiōnion.

paragraphs.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth on him should not perish, but have eternal life.
paragraphs.original: Οὕτως γὰρ ἠγάπησεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν κόσμον ὥστε τὸν υἱὸν τὸν μονογενῆ ἔδωκεν, ἵνα πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων εἰς αὐτὸν μὴ ἀπόληται ἀλλὰ ἔχῃ ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
paragraphs.translit: Houtōs gar ēgapēsen ho theos ton kosmon hōste ton hyion ton monogenē edōken, hina pas ho pisteuōn eis auton mē apolētai alla echē zōēn aiōnion.

paragraphs.text: For God sent not the Son into the world to judge the world; but that the world should be saved through him.
paragraphs.original: οὐ γὰρ ἀπέστειλεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν υἱὸν εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἵνα κρίνῃ τὸν κόσμον, ἀλλʼ ἵνα σωθῇ ὁ κόσμος διʼ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ou gar apesteilen ho theos ton hyion eis ton kosmon hina krinē ton kosmon, allʼ hina sōthē ho kosmos diʼ autou.

paragraphs.text: He that believeth on him is not judged: he that believeth not hath been judged already, because he hath not believed on the name of the only begotten Son of God.
paragraphs.original: ὁ πιστεύων εἰς αὐτὸν οὐ κρίνεται· ὁ δὲ μὴ πιστεύων ἤδη κέκριται, ὅτι μὴ πεπίστευκεν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ μονογενοῦς υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ho pisteuōn eis auton ou krinetai· ho de mē pisteuōn ēdē kekritai, hoti mē pepisteuken eis to onoma tou monogenous hyiou tou theou.

paragraphs.text: And this is the judgment, that the light is come into the world, and men loved the darkness rather than the light; for their works were evil.
paragraphs.original: αὕτη δέ ἐστιν ἡ κρίσις ὅτι τὸ φῶς ἐλήλυθεν εἰς τὸν κόσμον καὶ ἠγάπησαν οἱ ἄνθρωποι μᾶλλον τὸ σκότος ἢ τὸ φῶς, ἦν γὰρ αὐτῶν πονηρὰ τὰ ἔργα.
paragraphs.translit: hautē de estin hē krisis hoti to phōs elēlythen eis ton kosmon kai ēgapēsan hoi anthrōpoi mallon to skotos ē to phōs, ēn gar autōn ponēra ta erga.

paragraphs.text: For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, and cometh not to the light, lest his works should be reproved.
paragraphs.original: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ φαῦλα πράσσων μισεῖ τὸ φῶς καὶ οὐκ ἔρχεται πρὸς τὸ φῶς, ἵνα μὴ ἐλεγχθῇ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: pas gar ho phaula prassōn misei to phōs kai ouk erchetai pros to phōs, hina mē elenchthē ta erga autou·

paragraphs.text: But he that doeth the truth cometh to the light, that his works may be made manifest, that they have been wrought in God.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ποιῶν τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἔρχεται πρὸς τὸ φῶς, ἵνα φανερωθῇ αὐτοῦ τὰ ἔργα ὅτι ἐν θεῷ ἐστιν εἰργασμένα.
paragraphs.translit: ho de poiōn tēn alētheian erchetai pros to phōs, hina phanerōthē autou ta erga hoti en theō estin eirgasmena.

paragraphs.text: After these things came Jesus and his disciples into the land of Judea; and there he tarried with them, and baptized.
paragraphs.original: Μετὰ ταῦτα ἦλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν Ἰουδαίαν γῆν, καὶ ἐκεῖ διέτριβεν μετʼ αὐτῶν καὶ ἐβάπτιζεν.
paragraphs.translit: Meta tauta ēlthen ho Iēsous kai hoi mathētai autou eis tēn Ioudaian gēn, kai ekei dietriben metʼ autōn kai ebaptizen.

paragraphs.text: And John also was baptizing in Enon near to Salim, because there was much water there: and they came, and were baptized.
paragraphs.original: ἦν δὲ καὶ ὁ Ἰωάννης βαπτίζων ἐν Αἰνὼν ἐγγὺς τοῦ Σαλείμ, ὅτι ὕδατα πολλὰ ἦν ἐκεῖ, καὶ παρεγίνοντο καὶ ἐβαπτίζοντο·
paragraphs.translit: ēn de kai ho Iōannēs baptizōn en Ainōn engys tou Saleim, hoti hydata polla ēn ekei, kai pareginonto kai ebaptizonto·

paragraphs.text: For John was not yet cast into prison.
paragraphs.original: οὔπω γὰρ ἦν βεβλημένος εἰς τὴν φυλακὴν ὁ Ἰωάννης.
paragraphs.translit: oupō gar ēn beblēmenos eis tēn phylakēn ho Iōannēs.

paragraphs.text: There arose therefore a questioning on the part of John`s disciples with a Jew about purifying.
paragraphs.original: Ἐγένετο οὖν ζήτησις ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν Ἰωάννου μετὰ Ἰουδαίου περὶ καθαρισμοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Egeneto oun zētēsis ek tōn mathētōn Iōannou meta Ioudaiou peri katharismou.

paragraphs.text: And they came unto John, and said to him, Rabbi, he that was with thee beyond the Jordan, to whom thou hast borne witness, behold, the same baptizeth, and all men come to him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἦλθον πρὸς τὸν Ἰωάννην καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ῥαββί, ὃς ἦν μετὰ σοῦ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, ᾧ σὺ μεμαρτύρηκας, ἴδε οὗτος βαπτίζει καὶ πάντες ἔρχονται πρὸς αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēlthon pros ton Iōannēn kai eipan autō· Rhabbi, hos ēn meta sou peran tou Iordanou, hō sy memartyrēkas, ide houtos baptizei kai pantes erchontai pros auton.

paragraphs.text: John answered and said, A man can receive nothing, except it have been given him from heaven.
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰωάννης καὶ εἶπεν· Οὐ δύναται ἄνθρωπος λαμβάνειν οὐδὲ ἓν ἐὰν μὴ ᾖ δεδομένον αὐτῷ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē Iōannēs kai eipen· Ou dynatai anthrōpos lambanein oude hen ean mē ē dedomenon autō ek tou ouranou.

paragraphs.text: Ye yourselves bear me witness, that I said, I am not the Christ, but, that I am sent before him.
paragraphs.original: αὐτοὶ ὑμεῖς μοι μαρτυρεῖτε ὅτι εἶπον· Οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐγὼ ὁ χριστός, ἀλλʼ ὅτι Ἀπεσταλμένος εἰμὶ ἔμπροσθεν ἐκείνου.
paragraphs.translit: autoi hymeis moi martyreite hoti eipon· Ouk eimi egō ho christos, allʼ hoti Apestalmenos eimi emprosthen ekeinou.

paragraphs.text: He that hath the bride is the bridegroom: but the friend of the bridegroom, that standeth and heareth him, rejoiceth greatly because of the bridegroom`s voice: this my joy therefore is made full.
paragraphs.original: ὁ ἔχων τὴν νύμφην νυμφίος ἐστίν· ὁ δὲ φίλος τοῦ νυμφίου ὁ ἑστηκὼς καὶ ἀκούων αὐτοῦ, χαρᾷ χαίρει διὰ τὴν φωνὴν τοῦ νυμφίου. αὕτη οὖν ἡ χαρὰ ἡ ἐμὴ πεπλήρωται.
paragraphs.translit: ho echōn tēn nymphēn nymphios estin· ho de philos tou nymphiou ho hestēkōs kai akouōn autou, chara chairei dia tēn phōnēn tou nymphiou. hautē oun hē chara hē emē peplērōtai.

paragraphs.text: He must increase, but I must decrease.
paragraphs.original: ἐκεῖνον δεῖ αὐξάνειν, ἐμὲ δὲ ἐλαττοῦσθαι.
paragraphs.translit: ekeinon dei auxanein, eme de elattousthai.

paragraphs.text: He that cometh from above is above all: he that is of the earth is of the earth, and of the earth he speaketh: he that cometh from heaven is above all.
paragraphs.original: Ὁ ἄνωθεν ἐρχόμενος ἐπάνω πάντων ἐστίν. ὁ ὢν ἐκ τῆς γῆς ἐκ τῆς γῆς ἐστιν καὶ ἐκ τῆς γῆς λαλεῖ· ὁ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐρχόμενος ἐπάνω πάντων ἐστίν·
paragraphs.translit: Ho anōthen erchomenos epanō pantōn estin. ho ōn ek tēs gēs ek tēs gēs estin kai ek tēs gēs lalei· ho ek tou ouranou erchomenos epanō pantōn estin·

paragraphs.text: What he hath seen and heard, of that he beareth witness; and no man receiveth his witness.
paragraphs.original: ὃ ἑώρακεν καὶ ἤκουσεν τοῦτο μαρτυρεῖ, καὶ τὴν μαρτυρίαν αὐτοῦ οὐδεὶς λαμβάνει.
paragraphs.translit: ho heōraken kai ēkousen touto martyrei, kai tēn martyrian autou oudeis lambanei.

paragraphs.text: He that hath received his witness hath set his seal to [this], that God is true.
paragraphs.original: ὁ λαβὼν αὐτοῦ τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἐσφράγισεν ὅτι ὁ θεὸς ἀληθής ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: ho labōn autou tēn martyrian esphragisen hoti ho theos alēthēs estin.

paragraphs.text: For he whom God hath sent speaketh the words of God: for he giveth not the Spirit by measure.
paragraphs.original: ὃν γὰρ ἀπέστειλεν ὁ θεὸς τὰ ῥήματα τοῦ θεοῦ λαλεῖ, οὐ γὰρ ἐκ μέτρου δίδωσιν τὸ πνεῦμα.
paragraphs.translit: hon gar apesteilen ho theos ta rhēmata tou theou lalei, ou gar ek metrou didōsin to pneuma.

paragraphs.text: The Father loveth the Son, and hath given all things into his hand.
paragraphs.original: ὁ πατὴρ ἀγαπᾷ τὸν υἱόν, καὶ πάντα δέδωκεν ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ho patēr agapa ton hyion, kai panta dedōken en tē cheiri autou.

paragraphs.text: He that believeth on the Son hath eternal life; but he that obeyeth not the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God abideth on him.
paragraphs.original: ὁ πιστεύων εἰς τὸν υἱὸν ἔχει ζωὴν αἰώνιον· ὁ δὲ ἀπειθῶν τῷ υἱῷ οὐκ ὄψεται ζωήν, ἀλλʼ ἡ ὀργὴ τοῦ θεοῦ μένει ἐπʼ αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: ho pisteuōn eis ton hyion echei zōēn aiōnion· ho de apeithōn tō hyiō ouk opsetai zōēn, allʼ hē orgē tou theou menei epʼ auton.
